headline: No enforced disappearances or extrajudicial killings in last 6 months: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed
summary: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed made the remarks on the eve of the International Day of the Victims of Enforced Disappearances, also discussing a new law to address the issue.
details: Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated on Saturday that no one in Bangladesh has been subjected to enforced disappearance, extrajudicial killing, or political persecution since the current government took office six months ago.

He made these remarks at a panel discussion organized by Mayer Daak at the National Museum auditorium in Shahbagh, held on the eve of the International Day of the Victims of Enforced Disappearances. The event brought together victims of past disappearances and their families.

Addressing allegations concerning Miraj Sheikh's disappearance, the Home Minister said an independent investigation found no evidence of political motive. He suggested Miraj might have been caught in infighting among robber groups in the Sundarbans, noting a similar "record" for Miraj, his father, and grandfather.

Regarding the Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Redress Act 2026, the minister emphasized that merely forming a commission would not resolve the issue. The law aims to ensure every victim can approach the court for justice, outlining definitions, offenses, punishments, and investigation procedures.

The law includes provisions for heirs to receive property rights if a disappeared person does not return, along with compensation. A proposal also includes state compensation if perpetrators cannot pay, with the death penalty as the maximum punishment.

Salahuddin said the draft was prepared after discussions with stakeholders, UN representatives, diplomatic missions, and human rights bodies, aligning international standards with national realities. He noted that suggestions and amendments can still be submitted, and the law can be amended in the future.

Human rights activist Nur Khan Liton, however, raised concerns about Miraj Sheikh's case, citing eyewitness accounts and digital data indicating law enforcement involvement. He alleged that no effective legal action has been taken, and pressure is being applied on local people and witnesses.

Liton demanded a transparent probe into the roles of police and the Coast Guard in Miraj Sheikh's disappearance. He also stressed the paramount importance of ensuring an independent investigation within the framework of the new law.

headline_marked: [[Iran earns $7.5 billion from oil sales]] in four months despite US naval blockade
headline: Iran earns $7.5 billion from oil sales in four months despite US naval blockade
summary: Iran's central bank received $7.5 billion from oil sales in the first four months of the current fiscal year, defying US naval sanctions and meeting budget targets. This revenue will cover government foreign currency expenses from July to December.
details: Iran's central bank has received $7.5 billion from crude oil sales during the first four months of the current fiscal year (March-July). This information was reported by Iran's semi-official Fars news agency.

Despite a US naval blockade, Iran claims to have met its budget targets through these oil sales. The revenue is expected to cover the government's foreign currency expenditures from July to December, according to the Ministry of Petroleum.
This announcement comes amidst ongoing disruptions to Iran's oil exports and maritime trade due to the US naval blockade. The sanctions aim to restrict Iran's access to international markets.

The Strait of Hormuz remains a key flashpoint between Iran and the United States, as it is a crucial waterway for one-fifth of global oil transport. Iran has effectively closed this waterway since the start of the conflict.
The US, conversely, demands the Strait be kept open for free navigation. A memorandum of understanding was signed between Iran and the US in June to end the conflict.

Iranian officials state that Tehran will not fully reopen the Strait until Washington fulfills its commitments under the agreement. These commitments include lifting the naval blockade, releasing frozen Iranian assets abroad, and removing other sanctions.

Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian acknowledged the negative impact of US sanctions on the country's economy. He stated on state television that "We are in a war, and we have to accept this wartime situation."
Tehran Governor Mohammad Sadegh Motamedian further noted that Iran faces unprecedented challenges in governing the country during this conflict due to the naval blockade.
